source.title: Cross-Lingual Alignment Without Joint Training: Do Monolingual Language Models Converge on Universal Representations?
source.authors: Ej Zhou; Suchir Salhan; Catherine Arnett; Anna Korhonen

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests representational convergence using cross-lingual CKA, scaling comparisons, post-hoc mappings, and activation patching. It is a conceptual test of convergence rather than a reproduction of the original cross-modal method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own CKA comparisons, scaling results, reconstruction metrics, and patching outcomes. Cited findings from other work are not recorded. Detailed per-language-pair matrices, additional dataset-specific matrices, and many layerwise results are omitted in favor of reported aggregates and salient outcomes; see rows_left_out.
record.test_reason: The study measures cross-model representational alignment between independently trained monolingual LMs using linear CKA with shuffled controls, varying training-data tier, pooling and dataset. It fits Procrustes, affine and MLP maps and tests functional transfer by cross-model patching. These results bear directly on V1, V4, V6 and V7. It uses CKA rather than the original mutual-kNN metric, in a cross-lingual rather than cross-modal setting, so it is a different method aimed at the same question (T2; arguably also T3).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that independently trained monolingual LMs develop alignable geometry, that a single Procrustes rotation fit on parallel sentences maps between them, and that the same rotation transfers factual content in patching. They attribute the alignment to the structure of language and the world it describes rather than joint training. They also claim alignment strengthens with data scale, model scale and linguistic proximity, but model scale is not separately tested: it is confounded with data tier, and the ~1B set has no scale contrast.
record.recipe_differences: Uses linear CKA, as in representation-similarity work, but applies it to strictly monolingual cross-language models and varies training-data tiers. Adds Procrustes reconstruction and causal activation patching; this is not a reproduction of the original cross-modal setup.
record.method_sensitivity: CKA magnitude differs with pooling strategy and dataset; reconstruction rankings differ across retrieval, MSE, and CKA, and retrieval varies with candidate-pool definition and layer. Alignment also varies with language-pair typological distance.

fits_no_version.finding: Cross-size comparison: the same-language model at a different data size (1000 vs 100 MB; 10 vs 5 MB) aligns much more than cross-language pairs. For example, eng 1000 MB vs eng 100 MB scores 0.88 against 0.69–0.78 off-diagonal (Fig. 7).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Same-language models trained on different data amounts converge more than cross-language models (a within-language analogue of convergent learning).

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: Most controlled analyses use one model family with shared architecture and objective; parameter count is not isolated from data scale. Coverage is limited to nine main-analysis languages and approximately 1B independent models. Low-resource analyses are correlational only. Causal patching covers restricted factual cloze tasks, one concept-bearing span, and first-subword scoring. Some detailed outcomes are figure-only, and several small relation sets have wide, overlapping confidence intervals.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the full 36-pair CKA matrices for all datasets and pooling settings (Appendix Tables 11–22), detailed cross-size matrices (Appendix Figures 7–9), and most per-layer and per-pair reconstruction plots (Figures 10–13, 17–18). These add many separate cells but are not needed to represent the reported aggregate outcomes and main changes in conditions.

untested.parts: Parameter count is not varied independently of data. No models above ~1.5B are tested (7B+ untested). Objectives are shared across all models. The study does not compare larger vs smaller models within the independently developed set.
Entirely untested: no same-architecture seed comparisons.
Unpaired or unsupervised mapping, stitching layers and relative representations are untested. Multi-token generation is untested. Reconstruction and patching for low-resource languages are untested.
Entirely untested: no neuron, SAE-feature or circuit comparisons.
Neighbour-count settings, mutual-kNN metrics and out-of-distribution inputs are untested.
No scaling plateau test. The study does not separate the shared next-token objective from a common-reality explanation.

missing.what: Per-pair dataset dependence of CKA, e.g. eng–zho SGPT 0.82 FLORES vs 0.43 Tatoeba, and eng–hin 0.79 FLORES vs 0.34 OPUS. Some Tatoeba shuffled baselines are also inflated (spa–hin 0.65, rus–hin 0.63).
Goldfish vs Pythia-160M / Zh-Pythia-160M layerwise CKA: matched exceeds shuffled at every layer, but the profile is U-shaped with mid layers depressed.
Low-resource pairs (eng–tgl/swh/uzn/amh): matched−shuffled gaps of +0.39 to +0.58; Amharic shuffled is high at 0.41.
Post-Procrustes residual analysis: residual norm is 0.79–0.93 of the target's, high-rank, with 88–93% outside the target's top-10 directions.
Affine map fails in patching: the stricter Δd−Δt metric is negative, reflecting a magnitude artefact rather than directional transfer.
Training-corpus contamination audit: ≤0.1% English in the main corpora and up to 2.14% other-language text in low-resource corpora.
Predictor of alignment: joint regression shows syntactic distance adds ΔR²=.19 over NLL (p=.004). Genetic and geographic distances are also significant.

record.verdict_notes: Most comparator rows (r21–r30) should link to V4 only, not V6. Patching values in r35 come from a per-target choice of patch-start layer that maximises the result. The paper's statement that the three small relation sets merely 'directionally consistent' is contradicted for work→author and invention→inventor, whose CIs separate from shuffled. The study cites Gröger et al. and Koepke et al. on metric fragility, but those are cited results, not its own. Cross-architecture ~1B CKA (0.71) is not higher than 125M Goldfish CKA (0.76), so the study gives no evidence of convergence increasing with parameter scale.

versions.untested_parts: Data scale is varied and model quality is correlated with alignment, but parameter count is not independently varied while data and other factors are held fixed. Scaling beyond the tested tiers, including 7B+ models, is untested.
No vision-language model pairs or image-caption representations are tested.
The paper compares independently trained models across languages, not same-architecture training seeds or shared feature subspaces across seeds.

The rotations are fitted using parallel sentence pairs; unsupervised or unpaired mapping is not tested. Functional transfer is assessed on limited factual cloze tasks and first-subword answer scores, not broad downstream use or multi-token generation.
No recurring interpretable neurons, SAE features, or circuits are identified or compared.
The study varies pooling, datasets, and reconstruction metrics, but does not test neighbour-count settings or out-of-distribution inputs.

It reports incomplete functional transfer and effects of linguistic proximity, but does not isolate causal contributions of shared objectives versus a common model of reality, nor establish a scaling plateau.

rows.measure: Correlation of mean sentence NLL with CKA
rows.note: The authors interpret lower NLL, indicating better model fit, as associated with greater alignment.
rows.check: This is a correlation across language pairs at a fixed 1000 MB tier, not across model scale. NLL proxies how well each model learned its language and is entangled with language identity. Spearman ρ=−0.425, p=.010 (Table 7). The size field 'aggregate' is fine.

rows.measure: Correlation of syntactic distance with CKA
rows.note: Alignment varies with typological proximity; the paper reports syntactic distance as the strongest single predictor.
rows.check: This is a correlational predictor of alignment strength (syntactic distance ρ=−0.635). The URIEL distances are intercorrelated, and the authors do not dissociate them.
